title: Cipher Watch — Quick Runbook & Handoff
content:
Quick context (TL;DR):
This is a compact handoff for the overnight Cipher Watch shift. Meant to get you up to speed in ~5–10 minutes and provide quick mitigation paths for the two things that historically bite us overnight: KV cache runaway growth and batcher stalls causing token latency spikes.

Shift window: 23:30–07:30 PT
Primary channels: #ops-serving-runtime, #oncall-bridge, incident-runbook
Pager: ops-oncall (primary: oncall@pagerduty)
Priority contact: Ethan Cho (pager) -> Lina Alvarez (email)

Current state snapshot (last check 03:10 PT):
- Hosted API: green. 99th p50 token latency 310ms across r18.
- Dedicated pools: one pool (dedicated-gpu-3) at 78% utilization; autoscaler healthy.
- Recent deploy: canary for model ql6-3b-quant at 02:40 PT (canary -> 10% traffic). No errors flagged.
- Open incident: none escalated. There is a low-severity spike on KV cache memory in region eu-west-1 noted at 01:45 PT that resolved with cache-evict job.

Checklist — on takeover:
1) Check top-level dashboards: Console -> Serving -> Global overview (look for red cards).
2) Datadog quick queries:
   - Latency tail: avg(last_5m):avg:serving.request.latency{env:prod}.rollup(max, 60)
   - Error rate: sum:serving.errors{level:error}.rollup(sum, 60) by {route}
3) Verify autoscaler status for dedicated pools: kubectl get hpa -n serving | grep dedicated
4) Confirm canary health: /internal/canary/status (curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN")
5) Check KV cache memory goroutines: go-mem/kvcache exporter -> grafana panel "kvcache.heap_by_shard"
6) Check SLO alerts: Alertmanager UI -> firing?

Common night cruxes and playbook steps:
A) KV cache runaway (symptoms: mem pressure on inference nodes, OOM kills, tail latency climbs slowly):
   Quick indicators: increased "cache_items_total" and "cache_heap_bytes" spikes across multiple nodes; gc churn in node logs; eviction job triggered frequently.
   Immediate actions (fastest):
     - Kick manual eviction for hot-shards: curl -X POST https://internal-api/kvcache/evict?shard=<hot-shard> (use shard list from grafana panel).
     - If eviction doesn't reduce pressure in 90s, scale down cache shard retention: kubectl patch deployment kvcache --type json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/1/value","value":"48h"}]'
     - If OOMs continue, cordon the node and drain non-critical pods to reduce pressure: kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
   Follow-ups (next-day): open INF ticket with heap dumps, link to PR for improved eviction heuristics.

B) Batcher stall / token latency spike (symptoms: short window of 5–15 min high tail latency, worker backlog in queue, no corresponding CPU/GPU spike):
   Quick indicators: high "batcher.pending_requests", long-lived kernels in runtime logs, requests queued for >250ms.
   Immediate actions:
     - Check batcher telemetry: /metrics -> batcher_pending, batch_latency_histogram.
     - If pending_requests > threshold (default 250): restart the batcher worker on affected pods: kubectl rollout restart deployment/serving-batcher -n serving --field-selector metadata.name=<pod-name> (restart one at a time).
     - If restart not possible (ongoing deploy or maintenance), redirect traffic via routing policy: PATCH /api/routing/policy -> add rule route: low-priority -> route to smaller-seq-length model variant.
   Quick mitigation command sequence:
     1) kubectl -n serving get pods -l app=serving-batcher -o wide
     2) kubectl -n serving logs <pod> -c batcher --tail 200 | grep "pending_requests"
     3) kubectl -n serving exec <pod> -- kill -HUP 1   (graceful restart if restart is safe)
   Notes: prefer rolling a single batcher replica to avoid complete backlog collapse.

Escalation matrix (if step-up needed):
- Level 1: Oncall (you) -> resolve using runbook above.
- Level 2: Ethan Cho (pager) -> if cluster-wide memory or batcher restart doesn't remediate within 10 min.
- Level 3: Lina Alvarez (call) -> for incidents affecting >10% of traffic or sustained errors >15 min.
- Exec/Comms: Notify #status-updates and oncall@redwood-ops after Level 3.

Fast commands cheat-sheet: (paste into terminal)
- Check canary: curl -fsS https://internal/canary/status || echo "canary down"
- Top latency routes (Datadog): open dd -> dashboard "Serving -> Routes"
- Evict hot-shard: curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://internal-api/kvcache/evict?shard=shard-12
- Restart single batcher pod: kubectl -n serving rollout restart deployment/serving-batcher --selector=pod=<pod-name>

Notes on recent changes to watch for tonight:
- Canary deployment ql6-3b-quant (02:40 PT): watch for increased memory on canary nodes — they were built with the new 8-bit kernel.
- Autoscaler tweak rolled earlier today (INF-974) reduces cooldown to 45s; may cause flapping under bursty test traffic.

Outstanding TODOs for next shift (not blocking):
- Add a per-shard eviction debug endpoint to return last-10-evictions. (Owner: Lina)
- Formalize batcher restart SOP into infra-runbooks repo (PR open: #742). (Owner: Ethan)
- Add synthetic test that simulates slow consumer to catch batcher stalls.

Loose thoughts / notes to future self:
- Consider adding a soft cap on cache_items_per_client to reduce cross-tenant blast radius.
- Eviction job currently runs every 15m — maybe try 5m window in eu-west-1 only.

Link list / quick refs:
- Canary status page: https://console.redwood.com/internal/canary
- Eviction API: https://internal-api/kvcache/docs
- Datadog queries: https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/serving

If you take anything from this: prioritize stability > pushing canaries. If unsure, page Ethan early.

End of handoff — Maya (03:12 PT)

Unresolved questions to mention when you hand off:
- Did the loadtest team finish the Europe replay? If replay still running it will mask small regressions. (Slack: @loadtest-team)
- Is there any scheduled networking maintenance in eu-west-1 after 04:00 PT? I couldn't find a calendar entry.

-- scratch log (raw):
03:02 PT: noted small bump in kvcache.heap_by_shard -> shard-12 (evicted).
03:05 PT: triggered manual eviction for shard-12 (curl -> 200).
03:07 PT: latency back to baseline.
